nbzinbJia

nbzinbJia fits

  • negative binomial (NB2) regression with nbreg(), which reproduces MASS::glm.nb(), and
  • zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression with zinbreg(), which reproduces pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin").

Both models are estimated without any general-purpose optimizer (no optim(), nlm(), glm(), …):

Model Algorithm
NB IRLS (Fisher scoring) for β with θ fixed, alternated with Newton–Raphson for log θ with β fixed
ZINB EM algorithm: the E-step computes the posterior probability τᵢ that each zero is structural; the M-steps are a logistic IRLS fit with fractional response τᵢ (zero part) and the NB fit above with prior weights 1 − τᵢ (count part)

Standard errors for the ZINB model come from the analytic observed information matrix of (β, γ, log θ).

This package was written for the STA 651 final project (Miami University, Fall 2026).

Function reference website https://asahicn00.github.io/nbzinbJia/

The first implementation is preserved on the first-pass branch. The commits on main reconstruct the development steps from saved snapshots for the walkthrough.

Installation 

# install.packages(c("devtools", "remotes"))
devtools::install_github("AsahiCN00/nbzinbJia")

With devtools 2.5.0 or later, install_github() needs the remotes package (devtools no longer installs it automatically), so install it first if R asks for it. remotes::install_github("AsahiCN00/nbzinbJia") or pak::pak("AsahiCN00/nbzinbJia") work as well.

The package needs only stats and Formula. The examples and tests also use MASS, pscl, AER and numDeriv:

install.packages(c("MASS", "pscl", "AER", "numDeriv"))

Usage 

library(nbzinbJia)
data("bioChemists", package = "pscl")

# Negative binomial regression
nb <- nbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment, data = bioChemists)
summary(nb)
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)   0.2561     0.1373  1.8649   0.0622
#> femWomen     -0.2164     0.0726 -2.9795   0.0029
#> marMarried    0.1505     0.0821  1.8331   0.0668
#> kid5         -0.1764     0.0528 -3.3404   0.0008
#> phd           0.0153     0.0359  0.4257   0.6703
#> ment          0.0291     0.0032  9.0477   0.0000
#> Theta: 2.2644   Log-likelihood: -1560.958 on 7 Df

# Zero-inflated NB: count covariates | zero-inflation covariates
zinb <- zinbreg(art ~ fem + mar + kid5 + phd + ment | ment,
                data = bioChemists)
summary(zinb)$coefficients$zero
#>             Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)
#> (Intercept)  -0.8067     0.3532 -2.2840   0.0224
#> ment         -0.6095     0.2458 -2.4797   0.0131

# Model comparison and prediction
c(NB = AIC(nb), ZINB = AIC(zinb))
#>     NB   ZINB
#> 3135.9 3124.5

nd <- data.frame(fem = "Women", mar = "Married", kid5 = 0, phd = 3,
                 ment = c(0, 10, 30))
predict(zinb, newdata = nd, type = "zero")   # P(structural zero)
#>      1      2      3
#> 0.3086 0.0010 0.0000

Without |, zinbreg() uses the same covariates in both parts, as zeroinfl() does. Offsets can be given with the offset argument (count part) or with offset() in either part of the formula.

Main functions

Function Purpose
nbreg(), nbreg_control() NB regression and its tolerances / iteration limits / trace
zinbreg(), zinbreg_control() ZINB regression and its tolerances / iteration limits / trace

Both fitted classes ("nbreg", "zinbreg") have print, summary, coef, vcov, logLik (so AIC() and BIC() work), fitted, residuals ("response", "pearson"), nobs and predict (with newdata) methods. predict.zinbreg() supports type = "response" ((1 − π)μ), "count" (μ), "zero" (π) and "prob" (P(Y = k)).

Agreement with the reference implementations

Maximum absolute differences on pscl::bioChemists and AER::NMES1988 (checked in tests/testthat/):

NB vs glm.nb() ZINB vs zeroinfl()
Coefficients ≤ 5e-8 ≤ 2e-5
Standard errors ≤ 4e-10 ≤ 9e-6
θ (NB) / log θ (ZINB) ≤ 2e-8 ≤ 2e-6
Log-likelihood ≤ 7e-11 ≤ 2e-9
